claim: For the four-neuron BAM delay system (1.3) of Cui et al., linearized at the zero equilibrium, the characteristic determinant factors exactly as \(F(\lambda+a e^{-\lambda\theta})\), where \(F(z)=z^4+3z^2-z+1\). At the paper's Example 5.1 value \(a=1/4\), the complete set of positive imaginary-axis crossing frequencies is \(0.415764898027522\ldots\), \(0.705570557982711\ldots\), \(1.519025665632282\ldots\), and \(1.808831325587472\ldots\). The first crossing occurs at \(\omega_*=0.705570557982711\ldots\) and \(\theta_*=0.876243533775502\ldots\), with \(\operatorname{Re}(d\lambda/d\theta)=0.147965713761474\ldots>0\). Since the zero-delay characteristic polynomial is Hurwitz and no imaginary crossing occurs earlier, the zero equilibrium is linearly asymptotically stable for \(0\leq\theta<\theta_*\) and loses linear stability at \(\theta_*\). In particular, the source's reported \(\phi_0=2.0083\) is not an imaginary-axis crossing frequency for any delay at \(a=1/4\), and the exact first linear threshold is \(\theta_*\), rather than the reported numerical pair \(\phi_0=2.0083\), \(\theta_0\approx0.8\). This claim is only about the linear spectrum; it does not determine nonlinear Hopf criticality or the stability of any bifurcating periodic branch.
integrity: The determinant identity is exact; the threshold values are recomputed from the exact scalar factorization and checked independently by the bundled verifier. The reported source frequency is excluded by exhaustive enumeration of positive imaginary-axis crossing frequencies for \(a=1/4\).
scientific_limitations: The accepted claim concerns the linearized spectrum at the zero equilibrium for the printed common-delay model and specializes the numerical threshold to \(a=1/4\).
Nonlinear Hopf criticality, branch stability, and the hybrid-controlled system are not determined.
Published-literature comparison was targeted rather than an exhaustive inspection of every citing paper.
title: Exact factorization and corrected first delay crossing in a four-neuron BAM benchmark
